chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated, saying:
Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim used to say: “If you come to the Imam while he is sitting, having already prayed two rakʿahs, then pronounce the takbīr and sit down. Then when you stand up, pronounce the takbīr.”

key_terms.اجْلِسْ: sit down in accordance with the Imam’s state
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.جَالِسٌ: sitting, indicating the Imam’s current posture in prayer
key_terms.فَكَبِّرْ: say the takbīr, meaning to pronounce 'Allāhu Akbar'
key_terms.قُمْتَ: when you stand up to continue the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they join the Imam while he is sitting after two rakʿahs in congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical ruling about joining the congregational salat after the Imam has already completed two rakʿahs and is sitting. It instructs the follower to say the takbīr when joining and again when rising, showing the proper etiquette and form of participation in congregational prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1185 - Abdullah ibn al-Mughira narrated that

Mansur ibn Hazim used to say:
"If you come to the Imam and he is sitting, having already prayed two rak'ahs, say the takbir (Allahu Akbar) and then sit. When you stand up, say the takbir again."
